title: Tracing Recurrent and Emergent Hallucination Patterns in Decomposed Text-to-SQL Generation
abstract: arXiv:2610.27720v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models can achieve strong Text-to-SQL benchmark performance while still producing schema and query-logic errors. Most evaluations characterize such failures only in the final generated query, making it difficult to determine whether a related error was also observed in an earlier, simpler step or appears only at the final stage. We present a drill-down evaluation framework that decomposes Text-to-SQL queries into progressively more complex executable sub-queries and corresponding natural-language questions, allowing rule-based hallucination categories to be examined across a generation path. We distinguish recurrent hallucinations, in which the same rule-based category is observed in an earlier step and again in the final query, from emergent hallucinations, in which the category is observed at the final step without an earlier detection in the same path. translated_title: 在分解式Text-to-SQL生成中追踪复发性与涌现性幻觉模式
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型虽然能在Text-to-SQL基准测试中取得优异表现，但仍会产生模式（schema）错误和查询逻辑错误。大多数评估仅在最终生成的查询中刻画此类失败，因此难以判断相关错误是否在更早、更简单的步骤中就已经出现，还是仅在最终阶段才显现。我们提出了一个下钻式（drill-down）评估框架，将Text-to-SQL查询分解为复杂度逐步提升的可执行子查询以及对应的自然语言问题，从而能够在整条生成路径上检验基于规则的幻觉类别。我们区分了两类幻觉：“复发性幻觉”，即同一基于规则的类别在较早步骤中被观察到，并在最终查询中再次出现；“涌现性幻觉”，即该类别仅在最终步骤被观察到，而在同一路径的较早阶段未被检测到。在扩展的BIRD-mini基准上对五个大语言模型的评估中，……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一个下钻式评估框架，将Text-to-SQL生成过程分解为复杂度递增的可执行子查询，从而区分错误在早期步骤已出现并延续到最终查询的“复发性幻觉”与仅在最终查询才显现的“涌现性幻觉”，揭示大模型幻觉在生成路径中的演变规律。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a drill-down evaluation framework that decomposes Text-to-SQL generation into progressively more complex executable sub-queries, distinguishing "recurrent hallucinations" (errors detected in earlier steps and persisting to the final query) from "emergent hallucinations" (errors appearing only at the final step), thereby tracing how LLM hallucinations evolve along the generation path.
